items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Like for example I actually was at one where it was Red Rodney and Jay McShann, and things like that.

ctx.x: Just to wrap up, this weekend you’ll be playing with some pretty well-known musicians. Has there ever been any awkward moments at these? I know that the promoters, they kind of juggle people, they bring in all individuals, no bands really. And have you ever had a circumstance where the chemistry that they put together just hasn’t worked?

Yes that happens sometimes. But thankfully the sets are fairly short. I mean sometimes the promoters — this party actually I’ve seen the set list, and everything kind of works for this weekend. Because on this one, the musicians put together the sets. Jack Lesberg and Ralph Sutton do the sets. So they know who can play with who. But there were some famous ones a few years ago — I don’t know if I should mention names or not — but there was a famous promoter that almost started the jazz parties, and he used to put…
Sometimes you wonder, gee, how come this guy never made a record with that guy — because they’re all stars.
